raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What

Two independent fixes to the v1 inference norm kernels.

**1. Missing `threadsPerGroup==32` dispatch (layer_norm.cu, rms_norm.cu)**

`launch_fused_ln`, `launch_fused_residual_ln`, `launch_fused_residual_ln_store_pre_ln_res`, and `launch_rms_norm` all dispatch on `threadsPerGroup` with branches for {1, 2, 4, 8, 16} only. For `float32` inputs with `elems_per_row` in [65, 128], `T_per_load=4` gives `threadsPerGroup=32`, which falls through every branch — no kernel is launched and the output tensor holds uninitialized memory (silent numerical corruption).

Reproduced on MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.2): errors of 3–8 units for H=80–128 with `dtype=float32`.  
Fix: add `else if (threadsPerGroup == 32)` to all four dispatch tables.

Real-world trigger: per-head Q/K RMSNorm in EXAONE 4/4.5 with head_size 64 or 128 (related to #8886).

**2. ROCm 7.2.2 bf16 ABI build failure (conversion_utils.h)**

`conversion_utils.h` includes `cuda_bf16.h` guarded only by `BF16_AVAILABLE`. Hipify translates this to `hip_bf16.h` in `conversion_utils_hip.h`. When `op_builder` compiles `.cpp` files with plain `g++` and `-DBF16_AVAILABLE -D__HIP_PLATFORM_AMD__`, it pulls in `amd_hip_bf16.h`, which on ROCm 7.2.2 requires Clang-only builtins (`__builtin_elementwise_fma`, `__builtin_elementwise_ceil`, etc.) and a `__bf16` vector ABI not available under `g++`, causing the entire `inference_core_ops` extension to fail to build.

Fix: add `&& !defined(__HIP_PLATFORM_AMD__)` to match the identical pattern already in `ds_kernel_utils.h` (which has a comment explaining exactly this problem). Hipify will propagate the guard correctly to the generated `_hip.h` file.

## Test

Repro script for fix 1: verified H=80–128 (float32) produce zero error after the fix on gfx950.

+# Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+# DeepSpeed Team
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from deepspeed.accelerator import get_accelerator
+from deepspeed.inference.v2.kernels.core_ops import CUDAFPLN
+from ....v2.inference_test_utils import get_dtypes, allclose
+
+
+def reference_implementation(vals: torch.Tensor, gamma: torch.Tensor, beta: torch.Tensor,
+                             epsilon: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(vals.to(torch.float32), (vals.size(-1), ),
+                                          weight=gamma.to(torch.float32),
+                                          bias=beta.to(torch.float32),
+                                          eps=epsilon).to(vals.dtype)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.inference_v2_ops
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens, channels", [(1, 4096), (37, 2048), (64, 96), (64, 128)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", get_dtypes())
+def test_cuda_ln(tokens: int, channels: int, dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+    device = get_accelerator().current_device_name()
+    vals = torch.randn((tokens, channels), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    gamma = torch.randn((channels), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    beta = torch.rand((channels), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    epsilon = 1e-5
+
+    ref_output = reference_implementation(vals, gamma, beta, epsilon)
+
+    ln_kernel = CUDAFPLN(channels, dtype)
+    ds_output = torch.full_like(vals, float('nan'))
+    ln_kernel(ds_output, vals, gamma, beta)
+
+    assert allclose(ds_output, ref_output)

 @pytest.mark.parametrize("use_triton_ops", [False, True])
 def test_layer_norm(batch, seq_len, channels, dtype, use_triton_ops):
@@ -156,6 +156,33 @@ def test_layer_norm_residual_store_pre_ln_res(batch, seq_len, channels, dtype):
     assert allclose(ds_norm_output, ref_norm_output)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.inference_ops
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("channels", [96, 128, 1024])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.float32])
+def test_layer_norm_residual_kernels(channels, dtype):
+    # LayerNormOp.layer_norm_residual* are pure-PyTorch classmethods; call the kernels directly.
+    module = LayerNormOp().inference_module
+    device = get_accelerator().current_device_name()
+    vals = torch.randn((2, 32, channels), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    residual = torch.randn((2, 32, channels), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    bias = torch.randn((channels), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    gamma = torch.randn((channels), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    beta = torch.rand((channels), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    epsilon = 1e-5
+
+    # Plain layer_norm too: test_layer_norm skips when triton is unsupported.
+    assert allclose(module.layer_norm(vals, gamma, beta, epsilon),
+                    ref_implementation(vals, gamma, beta, epsilon, channels, dtype))
+
+    ref_norm, ref_res = residual_store_ref_implementation(vals, bias, residual, gamma, beta, epsilon, channels, dtype)
+
+    assert allclose(module._layer_norm_residual(vals, bias, residual, gamma, beta, epsilon), ref_norm)
+
+    ds_norm, ds_res = module.layer_norm_residual_store_pre_ln_res(vals, bias, residual, gamma, beta, epsilon)
+    assert allclose(ds_res, ref_res)
+    assert allclose(ds_norm, ref_norm)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.inference_ops
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("M", [4])
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("N", [4])
